summary: Bandai Namco's long-running action JRPG series, covering the seventeen mainline Tales entries and their major modern remasters/definitive releases.

entries.title: Tales of Phantasia

primary.version: Tales of Phantasia: Full Voice Edition / PSP route
primary.why: Phantasia has multiple later ports after the Super Famicom original; the PSP Full Voice line is the most complete high-fidelity legacy route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version with PPSSPP at increased internal resolution; use GBA only if official English is required.

secondary.what_to_play: Use the GBA version only if official English text is required.
secondary.why: The PSP versions were not the official Western release, while the GBA version was localized.

all_releases.reason: skip: superseded by later enhanced ports.

all_releases.fidelity: Legacy ports and localized GBA route.
all_releases.reason: secondary: GBA matters for official English, not fidelity.
primary: strongest legacy route for fidelity and completeness.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PSP is the best archive route, but GBA is the official English route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No current official PC/console remaster identified.

emulation.notes: Use PS2 emulation with increased internal resolution.

primary.why: The PS2 remake/Director's Cut is the most complete and highest-fidelity route for Destiny.
primary.how_to_play: Play Tales of Destiny Director's Cut with PCSX2 at increased internal resolution.

secondary.what_to_play: Use the PlayStation release if official English is required.
secondary.why: The PS2 remake/Director's Cut was not the official Western release.

all_releases.reason: secondary: official English route, lower fidelity than PS2 remake.
primary: most complete/highest-fidelity route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PS2 Director's Cut is best, but PlayStation is the official English route.

entries.title: Tales of Eternia

primary.why: Eternia's later PSP release is the highest-fidelity portable route; the PlayStation version remains the official North American Tales of Destiny II route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version with PPSSPP at increased internal resolution.

secondary.exclusive_content: Official North American localization under the title Tales of Destiny II.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the PlayStation version if the official North American script/release context matters.
secondary.why: The PSP route is the later version, while the PS1 release is the original localized route.

all_releases.reason: secondary: official localized route, lower fidelity than PSP scaling.
primary: best portable/fidelity route currently identified.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PSP is the fidelity route, while PS1 is the official North American route.

entries.remaster_caveats: A later remaster has not been officially sourced in this pass.

entries.title: Tales of Destiny 2

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for the PSP route or PCSX2 for PS2 comparison.

primary.why: The Japan-only true sequel to Destiny was released on PS2 and later PSP; PSP emulation is the cleanest modern route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version with PPSSPP, or use PCSX2 for the original PS2 release.

all_releases.reason: skip: original route, but PSP is the later portable version.
primary: clean modern emulation route for the later version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No official Western release or separate exclusive-content route identified.

entries.remaster_caveats: Japan/Asia-only title; do not confuse it with North America's renamed Tales of Eternia.

entries.title: Tales of Symphonia

emulation.notes: Use native Windows; Dolphin only for original GameCube comparison.

primary.why: Symphonia has GameCube, PS2, PS3, PC, and later remastered console routes; Windows provides the highest configurable fidelity for the content-complete post-PS2/Chronicles line.
primary.how_to_play: Play Tales of Symphonia on Windows/Steam with current patches.

all_releases.reason: skip: strong original route, but lacks later PS2/Chronicles content.

all_releases.fidelity: Later versions with added content and Chronicles collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: content route, but Windows has the stronger capture/fidelity path.
primary: highest configurable fidelity route.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered console release with enhanced graphics.
all_releases.reason: skip: modern console route, but not more configurable than PC.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: GameCube is a beloved original-performance route, while later ports carry added content; the archive pick favors PC for modern fidelity.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remastered console editions are useful, but PC remains the configurable route.
